title: Near-term demand stressmap and rollback schedule (Q4 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, operational sheet to (a) map near-term demand scenarios into region-level activation decisions, (b) define explicit rollback/mitigation windows for Q4 2026 soft-launches, and (c) capture unresolved capacity risk assumptions. This is intentionally concise — refer to the capacity playbook for background links.

Summary (one-line):
If week-over-week production token volume + new enterprise onboardings push estimated region utilization above the trigger thresholds in any two consecutive days, follow the rollback schedule below and activate contingency lanes.

Key assumptions (short):
- Baseline demand growth: 6% week-over-week for paid API traffic through Nov, 3% after product-seasonality taper in Dec.
- New enterprise onboards (expected): 4 deals in NA, 2 in EU, 1 in APAC between Oct 15–Nov 30 — each ~5M tokens/day steady-state.
- Typical model mix: 55% medium (Llama-3-70B-ish variants), 30% large (open-weights H100-friendly), 15% embeddings/rerank.
- GPU mix planned for activations: H100 (payg/reserved), A100-80 (reserved), L4 (for embeddings and small models).
- Warm-pool buffer targets: NA 8% of active fleet, EU 10%, APAC 16% (higher due to onboarding uncertainty).

Region-level forecast (next 12 weeks) — condensed table (numbers = active GPUs expected):
- NA (primary cloud zone): Week0 320 -> Week4 360 -> Week8 420 -> Week12 470 (scenario = base).
- EU (primary cloud zone): Week0 150 -> Week4 170 -> Week8 195 -> Week12 220.
- APAC (primary cloud zone): Week0 80 -> Week4 96 -> Week8 120 -> Week12 150.
Notes: these are *activations* not installed capacity; warm-pool and spot lanes are included in counts where labeled.

Three demand scenarios (short):
- Base: growth per assumptions above. Unit utilization targets 60% sustained for H100/A100 to meet cost SLO.
- High: +30% token volume (marketing / viral event) -> utilization spikes to 85% across primary GPUs for 2–5 days.
- Stress: +70% token volume or multiple enterprise onboards stacking -> sustained 90%+ utilization forcing immediate throttles/rollbacks.

Trigger thresholds (operational):
1) Alert level YELLOW: region average GPU utilization >=78% for 12h and queue length > 4s p95. Ops notify infra lead.
2) Alert level RED: region average GPU utilization >=88% for 2h OR error rate spike >1.5x baseline for >=30m. Immediate mitigation required.

Rollback & mitigation schedule (ordered, with ownership):
- Stage 0 (pre-emptive): Increase warm-pool eviction policy to 60s TTL, enable small-batch autoscale for embeddings. Owner: Benji Park.
- Stage 1 (YELLOW): Reduce max-concurrent-per-key to 0.9x current, move lower-priority customers to dedicated burst-backoff queue. Owner: Clara Martinez.
- Stage 2 (RED immediate): Canary rollback of last 24h canary routes (rollback percentage timeline: 100% -> 50% -> 10% over 30m). Freeze all new model rollouts. Owner: Dylan Cho.
- Stage 3 (regional degrade): Shift non-latency-critical requests to cheaper model-variants (quantized). Activate cross-region routing (NA -> EU or EU -> NA based on latency SLO flex). Owner: Evan Ross.
- Stage 4 (emergency): Engage on-call SRE to trigger spillover to reserved burst lane (pre-provisioned 120 GPUs across zones) and throttle incoming requests by token rate to capped T/s. Exec escalation if >6h. Owner: Infrastructure Pager.

Rollback windows and timing rules (operational playbook):
- If RED triggers, perform Stage 2 actions within 15m, Stage 3 within 45m, Stage 4 within 2h if no improvement. Document every action in incident doc and tag JIRA.
- Rollbacks should be batched: revert single canary PR at a time with 10m observation windows to avoid cascading regressions.

Warm-pool / spot usage plan (quick):
- Spot lanes used only for embeddings and low-priority batch generation; capacity in spot is not counted in SLA pool.
- Warm-pool targets by region (see above) with a policy to drain/prefill based on 6h signal. Rapidly prefilling warm pool if predicted incoming demand spike (probability >40% per demand model) — prefill schedule must be initiated 12h before expected spike.

Latency SLO mapping (short):
- 95p latency SLOs: NA <= 180ms for interactive, EU <= 230ms, APAC <= 300ms (soft). If cross-region routing used for capacity reasons, add 40ms penalty budget.

Risk register (compact):
- Risk A: Cloud vendor spot eviction during a sudden market event. Mitigation: maintain >= 6% covered reserved buffer + warm-pool. Owner: Benji Park.
- Risk B: Enterprise customers bring bursty RLHF workloads. Mitigation: require burst policy in contract + ingress rate limits per tenant. Owner: Clara Martinez.
- Risk C: Network egress limits in APAC region causing unexpected throttles. Mitigation: pre-validate with partner and shift bulk traffic to alternate zone. Owner: Evan Ross.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm finalized enterprise onboarding schedule with Sales for Oct/Nov — current numbers are best-effort; Sales sync scheduled 2026-08-20.
- Validate cold-start behavior for quantized variants under heavy eviction — need lab spike test by infra-performance. Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-3499.
- Decide on a single canonical runbook page ID to link in incident posts (we have duplicates across Confluence).

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Run a 72h synthetic spike sim in NA with +40% baseline for 3 discrete days; measure queue and p95 latencies. Owner: Dylan. Deadline: 2026-08-20.
2) Prefill APAC warm-pool by 24 GPUs as a precaution for late-Oct onboards. Owner: Benji. Deadline: 2026-08-22.
3) Update routing policy shorthand in API gateway to include explicit fallbacks to EU for non-sensitive tenants. Owner: Evan. Deadline: 2026-08-24.

Notes / shorthand: this is intentionally a compact ops-first sheet. If we need a polished forecast deck, I can convert to slides for review next week (preferably after the synthetic spike sim completes).

References: Confluence (capacity playbook), JIRA-INFRA-3421 (enterprise onboarding tracker), ops PR 778 for routing changes.

Document history: draft created 2026-08-15 by Aisha; edits: 2026-08-20 (added warm-pool numbers), 2026-09-02 (clarified rollback timing).
